body.statement: Let \(\mu\) be a Borel probability measure on \(\mathbb R^k\), where \(k\geq0\), and let \(h\in\mathbb R^k\).  If translation by \(h\) preserves \(\mu\), then \(h=0\).  Consequently, if \(\mathcal L(Z+u)=\mathcal L(Z+v)\) for an \(\mathbb R^k\)-valued random vector \(Z\), then \(u=v\).
body.proof_tex:
The assertion is immediate for \(k=0\).  Suppose \(k>0\) and, toward a contradiction, \(h
e0\).  Push \(\mu\) forward by the linear functional \(z\mapsto h^{\mathsf T}z/\lVert hVert\).  The resulting probability measure \(
u\) on \(\mathbb R\) is invariant under translation by \(r=\lVert hVert>0\).  The half-open Borel intervals
\[
 I_m=[mr,(m+1)r),\qquad m\in\mathbb Z,
\]
are pairwise disjoint, cover \(\mathbb R\), and all have the same \(
u\)-mass \(c\).  If \(c>0\), countable additivity gives \(
u(\mathbb R)=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}c=\infty\); if \(c=0\), it gives \(
u(\mathbb R)=0\).  Both conclusions contradict \(
u(\mathbb R)=1\).  Hence \(h=0\).  For the consequence, translating \(\mathcal L(Z+u)=\mathcal L(Z+v)\) by \(-v\) shows that \(\mathcal L(Z)\) is invariant under translation by \(u-v\), so the first part gives \(u=v\).
